panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: MRI row from 9 April 2025 shows extensive left skull base/nasopharyngeal mass with dural and perivertebral extension and sigmoid sinus thrombosis in a case report of atypical skull base osteomyelitis filed under necrotizing otitis externa; the caption does not describe external auditory canal disease, so the disease attribution is inferential and low confidence. [raw subtype: skull_base_osteomyelitis] b: Follow-up MRI (30 April 2025) of the same skull base lesion after antibiotic therapy; same limited disease attribution as row a. [raw subtype: skull_base_osteomyelitis] c: Third MRI time point (26 June 2025) of the same skull base lesion; disease attribution to necrotizing otitis externa remains inferential from the article-level case assignment. [raw subtype: skull_base_osteomyelitis]
panels.attribution_text: Stocker et al. Atypical Skull Base Osteomyelitis of the Clivus Mimicking a Malignant Lesion: A Case Report.. Diseases (Basel, Switzerland) 2026. doi:10.3390/diseases14040138. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Exemplary representation of the MRI scans the patient received from April until June 2025. Axial images are represented on the left, sagittal images on the right. The first column of axial images consists of contrast-enhanced maximum intensity projection (MIP), the second column of axial images consists of native T2 images, the first column of sagittal images of b and c are contrast-enhanced compressed sensing T1 images, the sagittal image of c is a native compressed sensing T1 image, and the second column of sagittal images are native T1 images. (a) MRI scan from 9 April 2025 showing an extensive, malignant-suspicious mass lesion in the skull base/nasopharynx on the left side (black and white asterisk). Furthermore, broad-based involvement of the dura (white arrow) and ossary involvement/partial destruction and extensive perivertebral contrast accumulation caudally up to C2 (yellow star) are described, as well as partial sinus vein thrombosis affecting the left sigmoid sinus (blue arrow). (b) MRI scan from 30 April 2025 showing the known lesion with slightly regressive contrast enhancement but unchanged extent of the lesion (black and white asterisk). (c) MRI scan from 26 June 2025 showing the known lesion in the left nasopharynx, tending to decrease in intensity but with slightly increasing signal on the right side (black and white asterisk).
in_text_mentions: A follow-up MRI scan two weeks after initiation of antibiotic therapy revealed a decrease in the size of the osteomyelitic lesion but an increasingly hyperintense representation of the cervical soft tissues on the left paramedian and dorsal to the atlas. Consecutive MRI scans are depicted in Figure 2.

source_variant.figure_caption: Exemplary representation of the MRI scans the patient received from April until June 2025. Axial images are represented on the left, sagittal images on the right. The first column of axial images consists of contrast-enhanced maximum intensity projection (MIP), the second column of axial images consists of native T2 images, the first column of sagittal images of b and c are contrast-enhanced compressed sensing T1 images, the sagittal image of c is a native compressed sensing T1 image, and the second column of sagittal images are native T1 images. (a) MRI scan from 9 April 2025 showing an extensive, malignant-suspicious mass lesion in the skull base/nasopharynx on the left side (black and white asterisk). Furthermore, broad-based involvement of the dura (white arrow) and ossary involvement/partial destruction and extensive perivertebral contrast accumulation caudally up to C2 (yellow star) are described, as well as partial sinus vein thrombosis affecting the left sigmoid sinus (blue arrow). (b) MRI scan from 30 April 2025 showing the known lesion with slightly regressive contrast enhancement but unchanged extent of the lesion (black and white asterisk). (c) MRI scan from 26 June 2025 showing the known lesion in the left nasopharynx, tending to decrease in intensity but with slightly increasing signal on the right side (black and white asterisk).
